findings.title: Cache is not re-checked after acquiring the write lock (incomplete double-checked locking)
findings.body: GetWebAssets first reads entryPointAssetsCache under a read lock (lines 41-43), then acquires the write lock at line 48 and unconditionally reloads the manifest from disk (readWebAssetsFromFile at line 60) and republishes the cache. Because there is no second check after the write lock is acquired, any requests that arrive concurrently before the cache is first populated will each perform the full manifest load sequentially and overwrite each other's cache entry. Besides duplicated disk I/O, a transient read error in a later goroutine can replace an already-populated good cache entry with nil and return an error to its caller even though a valid cached value existed. The standard fix is to re-check `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }` immediately after taking the write lock.

findings.title: Write lock is held across manifest file I/O, serializing all GetWebAssets callers
findings.body: The deferred Unlock at line 49 keeps entryPointAssetsCacheMu held while readWebAssetsFromFile (line 60) opens, reads, and parses assets-manifest.json from disk. While the write lock is held, every other goroutine calling GetWebAssets blocks — including callers that would otherwise be served by the read-locked fast path, since RLock cannot proceed while the write lock is held. In dev mode (setting.Dev) the fast path is skipped by design, so every index page load now serializes on this disk I/O, and on a slow filesystem all such requests stall behind a single global mutex. Loading and parsing the manifest outside the lock and only taking the write lock to publish the result would avoid this.

findings.title: No regression test for the data race this PR fixes
findings.body: The PR adds a mutex to guard the package-level entryPointAssetsCache but adds no test. A data-race fix without a test that exercises concurrent access can silently regress. A test that calls GetWebAssets from multiple goroutines against a temporary assets-manifest.json (with cfg.Env set to a non-dev value so the cache path is exercised) and is run with the race detector enabled (`go test -race`) would have caught the original race and would verify the fix going forward.
